Nobody Wants This Ford Mustang Boss 302, Muscle Car Has One Owner in the Papers, 520 Miles Shown
16 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
Are you still thinking about sprucing up your life with a cool, modern-classic muscle car, but find the latest S650 Ford Mustang and its predecessor, the S550, a bit too bland, and not that cool? Well, in that case, how about an S197?
This is the code for the fifth-generation model, which was assembled between 2004 and 2014. Production took place at the Flat Rock factory in Michigan, USA. The company offered it in two body styles, a two-door coupe and a two-door convertible, and the S197 II was offered with a pair of V6 engines, as well as several V8s. The engine family included the 5-liter Coyote, as well as a pair of supercharged units, and depending on the spec, they were offered with manual and automatic transmissions.
Pictured above is a 2013 Ford Mustang Boss 302 , a model that came with the usual Coyote V8, albeit in an enhanced version, featuring plenty of modifications. The output was rated at 444 horsepower (450 ps/331 kW), and the thrust was 380 pound-feet (515 Nm). Various tests from back in the day revealed that the 0-60 mph (0-97 kph) took a little over 4 seconds, and the quarter mile was dealt with in just over 12 seconds. The top speed was capped at (155 mph (250 kph), but the model could easily exceed it.
A six-speed manual transmission channels everything to the rear wheels, and besides the extra oomph, this model also featured a modified chassis setup, sat a bit closer to the asphalt, rode on 19-inch alloys, and came with a special aero package inspired by the Boss302R racer. Some of the goodies included the Bluetooth connectivity, a premium audio system, power-adjustable seats at the front, SiriusXM, and others. The Sync system was added on later models.
Photo: Cars&Bids According to the listing, the Ford Mustang Boss 302 in question comes with the factory wheels, has a 3.73:1 limited-slip rear axle, a manually adjustable suspension, Brembo brakes at the front, stripes on the hood and profile, air conditioning, cruise control, and an Alcantara-wrapped steering wheel. It has a Race Red exterior, a Charcoal Black cabin, a clean Texas title, and is located in Willis, TX.
And it has been living in Texas its entire life, because it has a single owner in the papers, and this definitely adds up to the hype. The vendor represents the first and only owner, and it is unknown why they want their muscle car gone, though they have probably gotten bored with it. This machine was $42,995 new, according to the attached window sticker, and this model is now worth from over $30,000 to roughly $50,000, depending on the usual factors that influence a car’s value.
It is worth noting that the tires on this 2013 Ford Mustang Boss 302 carry 2011 date codes on them, and this is something that the next owner will have to take care of, especially if they want to enjoy the vehicle in the open. The odometer read only 520 miles (~840 km) at the time of cataloging, but it is inaccurate. The vendor blames it on a clerical error, and says that they have filed a dispute claim with Carfax.
Photo: Cars&Bids Besides the muscle car, the next owner will also get the OEM car cover, one key, one red key, and the owner’s manual. And you know what to do if you want it, don’t you? Actually, you don’t, not yet, anyway, because we haven’t revealed this aspect yet. This ride was advertised on Cars&Bids as part of an auction that ended on November 2, 2026. When the gavel hit the table, the highest bid was $37,250. And since the reserve was not met, the muscle car failed to change hands.
As a result, we can assume that the seller likely wants more than $40,000, and it is up to you to decide whether it is worth that kind of money or not. Nevertheless, the chances of encountering a 2013 model year Ford Mustang Boss 302 with a single owner in the papers since new are close to zero, and if this matters, then you may want to make an offer. After all, what is the worse than they can do? Decline it?
The red-on-black vehicle with its clean Texas title and one owner in the papers, as well as the mileage discrepancy mentioned above, is still for grabs, and if you really want it, then you should get in touch with the vendor by accessing this link , which will redirect you to the quoted website. But before clicking that link, let us know how much this 2013 Ford Mustang Boss 302 is really worth in your opinion by dropping a line (or more) in the comments section at the bottom of the page. Keep in mind that it failed to sell for $37,250.
